target.title: fix(gateway): detect C1 control characters in config lookup path sanitizer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sanitizeLookupPathForLog()` in `src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts` replaces control characters in a config path with `?` before the path is embedded in the gateway warning logs (`config.schema.lookup produced invalid payload for ...` and `config.openFile failed path=...`). It only replaced the C0 range (0x00-0x1f) and DEL (0x7f), not the C1 control range (0x80-0x9f), which includes the CSI introducer U+009B — an alternative ANSI escape prefix equivalent to `ESC [`. A C1 byte in the path therefore passed unchanged into both warning-log callers.

## Change

Extend the replacement predicate to also cover 0x80-0x9f:

```ts
return code < 0x20 || code === 0x7f || (code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f) ? "?" : char;
```

## Testing / Proof

Added a regression to the existing `config.openFile` suite in `src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts`. It drives the real `config.openFile` handler with a config path containing U+009B, forces an open failure, and asserts the emitted `logGateway.warn` message replaces the C1 byte with `?` (`cfg?.json`) and contains no raw C1 byte. The assertion is scoped to the sanitized filename so it is independent of the OS-specific path prefix.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts
...
      Tests  8 failed | 14 passed (22)
```

The new `replaces C1 control characters in the logged failed config path` test passes (passed count rises from 12 → 14, i.e. +1 in each of the two gateway vitest projects).

> Note on the 8 "failed": these are 4 pre-existing sibling `config.openFile` tests (× 2 projects) that hard-code POSIX `/tmp/...` paths and assert the full path string. On my local **Windows** checkout the handler resolves those to `D:\tmp\...`, so they fail identically on `main` — they are unrelated to this change and pass on Linux CI. This PR's new test deliberately avoids the path prefix and asserts only the sanitized `cfg?.json` fragment, so it is green on both platforms.

target.title: fix(agents): adopt orphaned managed worktrees left by a crash between git worktree add and registry insert
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway crash (OOM kill, forced restart) landing between `git worktree add` and the registry insert inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves an on-disk worktree and an `openclaw/<name>` branch that no managed API can ever see, repair, or remove: `list()`/`get()` never show it, every `gc()` pass skips it forever, and any later `create()` with the same name fails hard with `branch already exists`. The only way out today is manual operator surgery (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) outside the managed API. Reported with source-level analysis in #103239; this PR makes the orphan self-heal (gc adopts it; a retried create adopts it and preserves the caller's owner) while leaving foreign/detached worktrees untouched.

## Summary

- Problem: A crash between `git worktree add` and `insertRegistryWorktree()` inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves a live git worktree + `openclaw/<name>` branch with no registry row. `reconcileOrphans()` explicitly skips it forever (invisible to `list()`/`gc()`), and a retried `create()` with the same name dead-ends on `branch already exists`.
- Why it matters: In real deployments (OOM kill, forced restart) the orphan is permanently unrecoverable through the managed API — only manual `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` unblocks the name.
- What changed: `reconcileOrphans()` now adopts live-but-unregistered worktrees back into the registry when — and only when — the directory is git-listed at that exact path on exactly the managed branch (`refs/heads/openclaw/<dirname>`); gc-side adoption is registration-only (background gc must not execute repo setup scripts), making the orphan visible/removable rather than silently trusted. `create()`'s branch-exists guard self-heals the same exact orphan signature instead of throwing: it re-runs `copyIncludedFiles()` + `runSetupScript()` with the normal create() failure semantics (on failure: `cleanupFailedCreate()` + rethrow; the registry row is inserted only after provisioning succeeds), preserves the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId`, and records the real resolved base (`resolveBase(repoRoot, params.baseRef)`) rather than a placeholder — because the crash window between `git worktree add` and the registry insert also spans `copyIncludedFiles()`/`runSetupScript()`, so an adopted worktree may be half-provisioned and a retried `create()` must re-establish create()'s post-conditions. `git.ts` additively parses the porcelain `branch` field.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): foreign/detached-HEAD worktrees keep today's preserve-but-don't-touch behavior (locked in by the existing test); no changes to `remove()`, snapshots, registry schema, CLI output, or `ManagedWorktreeGcResult` shape.

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker/verifier agents, human-operated); every change was gated on tests written first and independently reviewed by a fresh-context model before submission.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #103239
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: `create()` performs the irreversible git-side effects (`git worktree add`, branch creation) before the registry insert, with no crash-window reconciliation: `reconcileOrphans()` treated "git still lists this directory as a live worktree" purely as a preserve signal and never checked whether the worktree matches the managed naming scheme but lacks a registry row.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no adopt-or-repair path for the crashed-create signature; `create()`'s branch-exists guard had no way to distinguish "user's foreign branch" from "our own crashed create()".
- Contributing context (if known): the registry has no `name` column (name derives from the path's last segment), so adoption needs no extra bookkeeping — the orphan is fully re-derivable from path + branch.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [ ] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: a live worktree + managed branch with no registry row (the exact end-state of a crash between `git worktree add` and the registry insert) is (a) adopted by `gc()` into `list()` with matching path/branch and not deleted from disk, and (b) adopted by a retried `create()` with the same name — preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId` so `findLiveByOwner()` and idle-gc semantics keep working — instead of throwing `branch already exists`; (c) a retried `create()` after a crash BEFORE setup completed re-runs provisioning (restores `.worktreeinclude`-copied files and the setup-script marker, records the real `baseRef`); and (d) a setup script that fails during adoption-retry makes `create()` throw and leaves no worktree, branch, or registry row behind.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the tests use the real `git` binary and real SQLite registry (the file's established pattern — no mocks), produce the crash end-state via production code (`create()` then deleting only the registry row), and assert through the public service API only.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): "deletes unregistered orphan debris but preserves git-listed worktrees" covers the foreign/detached case and stays green, locking in that non-managed worktrees are never claimed.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A — two new tests added.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- `openclaw worktrees gc` (and the hourly automatic gc) now re-registers managed worktrees orphaned by a crashed `create()` instead of leaving them invisible forever.
- A retried `create()` with the same name after such a crash now succeeds (returns the adopted record) instead of failing with `branch already exists`.
- Foreign or detached-HEAD worktrees are unaffected.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> gc()/reconcileOrphans(): "git lists it" -> skip forever (invisible)
  -> create(same name): "branch already exists" (dead end)

After:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> gc()/reconcileOrphans(): exact path+branch match on openclaw/<name> -> adopt into registry
  -> create(same name): exact orphan signature -> adopt (owner preserved) -> returns record
  -> foreign/detached worktree -> preserved untouched (unchanged)
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A. Adoption is gated on an exact `git worktree list --porcelain` path + `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>` branch match; fabricating that state requires local filesystem/git access equivalent to what `create()` already requires. `insertRegistryWorktree` is the same call path `create()` already uses.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 26 (arm64); fix is platform-independent (pure git + SQLite service logic)
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / bun, source checkout
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): default `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`-backed state

### Steps

1. `ManagedWorktreeService.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` and kill the process after `git worktree add` completes but before the registry insert (repro: create normally, then delete only the registry row — identical end state).
2. Run `service.gc()`.
3. Run `service.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` again.

### Expected

- gc adopts the orphan (visible in `list()`, not deleted); retried create succeeds.

### Actual

- Before this PR: gc skips it forever; retried create throws `branch already exists: openclaw/task-1`. After this PR: expected behavior (see tests).

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Before (tests added, fix stashed):

```
❯ |agents| src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts (24 tests | 2 failed)
FAIL … adopts a worktree orphaned when create() crashed …, during gc()
  AssertionError: expected undefined to match object {…}
FAIL … adopts an orphaned worktree instead of throwing on a retried create() …
  Error: branch already exists: openclaw/orphan-retry
```

After:

```
pnpm test src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  27 passed (27)
```

Real-behavior proof (after-fix run through the actual service recovery path, genuine `kill -9` inside the crash window — exit 137 — against a real git repo + real SQLite registry, covering both the retried-create adoption with re-provisioning and the gc registration-only adoption): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103390#issuecomment-4937129438

Also green on the touched surface: `pnpm tsgo:core` (exit 0), `oxlint` (0 findings), `oxfmt --check` (formatted). Note: repo-wide `pnpm check` currently fails in its preflight `npm shrinkwrap guard` on an unmodified `origin/main` checkout in this environment (`ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` for the `defu` override) — pre-existing and unrelated; no lockfile/override files are touched by this PR.

Known narrow edges deliberately left out of scope (documented for reviewers): (1) `worktrees.path` has no UNIQUE constraint, so a gc racing an in-flight `create()` in the pre-insert window could double-insert — same pre-existing assumption that gc/create aren't concurrent for one path; (2) a lingering *removed* registry row at the same path still blocks create()-side adoption for a fresh orphan (name-reuse-after-remove + crash sequence).

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: full scoped test suite (25/25) against real git + real SQLite locally, including both new adoption tests and the pre-existing foreign-worktree preservation test; typecheck/lint/format on the touched files.
- Edge cases checked: detached-HEAD foreign worktree (preserved), bare branch collision without a live worktree (still throws), owner preservation (`workboard`/`ownerId`) on retried-create adoption including `findLiveByOwner()` lookup, crash-before-setup retry re-provisioning (include file + setup marker restored, real base recorded), and full cleanup on a failing setup script during adoption-retry.
- What you did **not** verify: a literal `kill -9` mid-`create()` on a production gateway (the crash end-state is reproduced through the service's own code paths instead); the two out-of-scope narrow edges above.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: adopting a worktree that a user intentionally created outside the managed API at the exact managed path on an `openclaw/<name>` branch.
  - Mitigation: that state is indistinguishable from (and equivalent to) a crashed managed create; adoption only registers it — it never deletes or modifies the worktree.
- Risk: gc racing an in-flight create() could double-insert a row for one path (no UNIQUE constraint on path).
  - Mitigation: window is the sub-second pre-insert gap and requires concurrent gc + create on the same repo; behavior before this PR already assumed these don't interleave; `list()` self-heals rows whose paths disappear.

# PR1/5 — docs/RFC/root-cause/boundary anchor

## Context capsule

This PR is item 1 of the rebuilt 2026.7.1 beta 3 durable core stack. It asks reviewers to evaluate the docs/RFC/root-cause/boundary anchor slice on its own base while recognizing that later PRs build cumulatively on top.

## Durable core stack overview

Durable core is the shared, opt-in runtime substrate that records accepted work identity, ordered steps and events, parent/child links, bounded refs, recovery states, wake/attention obligations, delivery evidence, and read-only inspection for long-running OpenClaw agent/session/task/subagent work. It is needed because 2026.7.1 beta 3 failures are cross-cutting: coordinator silence, restart/interruption loss, stale running work, parent/child handoff gaps, delivery/attention uncertainty, and side-effect uncertainty cannot be solved cleanly by one product surface alone.

The core is intentionally below Task Flow, Workboard, plugins, sessions, and channel UI. Those surfaces may project from durable facts, but they should not own the persistence boundary. This PR is docs/RFC only: it defines the value, root-cause model, and proof boundary before implementation PRs claim runtime behavior.

- PR1/5 — docs/RFC/root-cause/boundary anchor and proof plan.
- PR2/5 — runtime foundation/core plus terminal SQLite row immutability guard.
- PR3/5 — wake targets, durable producers, replay/resume semantics.
- PR4/5 — controls/inspection plus CLI/Gateway surface.
- PR5/5 — internal session delivery handoff, final hardening, and cumulative E proof.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): use truncateUtf16Safe for web snapshot maxChars cap
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `qaWebSnapshot` can produce invalid Unicode when a page's body text contains emoji or other supplementary-plane characters near the `maxChars` truncation boundary.

`qaWebSnapshot` caps the body text returned to QA scenarios with `text.slice(0, maxChars)`. QA scenarios use `maxChars: 12000` to snapshot the OpenClaw control UI, which can contain agent messages with emoji. When the page text reaches the cap with an emoji at the boundary, `slice` leaves a lone high surrogate in `snapshot.text` — which is then passed through `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` and used in `text.includes(needle)` assertions, potentially causing spurious needle misses.

**Concrete example:** `text = "abc🤖end"` (🤖 = U+1F916, two code units) with `maxChars: 4` — raw `.slice(0, 4)` keeps `"abc" + U+D83E`, a lone high surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `text.slice(0, maxChars)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, matching the established pattern used across `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts`, and others. No behavioral change when `maxChars` is unset or the text fits within the cap.

## User Impact

**Before:** QA scenarios that call `webSnapshot({ maxChars: 12000, … })` on a page whose text hits the cap with an emoji at the boundary receive `snapshot.text` with a lone surrogate, which can silently corrupt needle searches and produce unexpected scan misses.

**After:** `snapshot.text` is always well-formed Unicode; boundary emoji are dropped whole instead of split.

## Evidence

- `extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.ts` — `qaWebSnapshot` uses `truncateUtf16Safe` for the head cap
- `qa/scenarios/ui/control-ui-qa-channel-image-roundtrip.yaml` — live QA scenario using `webSnapshot({ maxChars: 12000, … })` with emoji needle checks as canonical reachability
- `src/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime.ts` — exports `truncateUtf16Safe` as a proper SDK subpath for bundled plugins
- Regression: `extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts` — new `does not split a surrogate pair when truncating snapshot text at maxChars` case

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `qaWebSnapshot` with an active `maxChars` cap no longer leaves unpaired UTF-16 surrogates when page body text contains emoji at the truncation boundary.
- **Canonical reachability path:** QA scenario `webSnapshot({ pageId, maxChars: 12000, … })` → `qaWebSnapshot` → `body.textContent()` → `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)` → `snapshot.text` → `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(snapshot.text).includes(needle)` in scenario assertion.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; no real browser needed — `bodyLocator.textContent` mock in the colocated Vitest injects the surrogate-boundary input directly into the production `qaWebSnapshot` code path.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `truncateUtf16Safe` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`; no provider/channel constraints — this is plugin-local web snapshot text handling.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node v22, branch `fix/qa-lab-web-snapshot-utf16`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
# 1. Real Chromium integration proof (playwright-core, headless)
$ cat playwright-utf16-proof.mts   # proof script (runs from repo root)

target.title: fix(agents): detect full C1 range in image-generate inline directive check
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sanitizeInlineDirectiveText()` in `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.ts` escapes control characters in provider/model/override text before generated-media directives are appended to the image-tool summary (so untrusted values can't inject `MEDIA:` directives or terminal escapes). Its `isInlineDirectiveControlCharacter()` predicate covered C0 (0x00-0x1f), DEL (0x7f), LS (0x2028) and PS (0x2029), but not the C1 control range (0x80-0x9f) — which includes the CSI introducer U+009B, an alternative ANSI escape prefix equivalent to `ESC [`.

## Change

Add `(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` to `isInlineDirectiveControlCharacter`, so C1 bytes are escaped to a visible backslash-u sequence alongside the existing ranges.

## Testing / Proof

Extended the existing summary-escaping regression in `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts` ("escapes image-generation summary text before appending tool MEDIA output") so an `ignoredOverrides` value now carries a U+009B control byte (followed by `[2J`). The test asserts the emitted summary contains the escaped backslash-u form of U+009B rather than the raw byte, while the structured `details` object still round-trips the original raw value unchanged.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts

target.title: refactor(agents): converge CLI tool terminal reason onto run-termination
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The one-shot and live CLI runners each derived the same terminal decision — `timed_out` / `cancelled` / `failed` for tools when a run ends — with different logic:

- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts` (one-shot) read the abort signal's lifecycle fields, then only recognized `FailoverError` timeouts; a `TimeoutError`-shaped or `AbortError`-shaped run error without an aborted signal classified as `failed`.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.ts` (live) only sniffed error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) and never consulted the abort signal.

Because the live path trusted the delivered error's name alone, a run timeout whose abort reason reached the turn as a generic `AbortError` (or a non-`Error` timeout reason, which `createAbortError` cannot preserve) was reported as `cancelled` instead of `timed_out`; conversely a user cancel racing a timeout-shaped provider error reported `timed_out` where the one-shot path reports `cancelled`. Same decision, two encodings, observable drift — seam 3 of #104219.

## Why This Change Was Made

Converge the derivation onto one owner, per the #104219 change shape. `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` lives in `src/agents/run-termination.ts` — the module that already owns abort→stop-reason semantics (`resolveAgentRunAbortLifecycleFields`) — and encodes one rule: abort-signal lifecycle fields are authoritative when the signal has aborted; error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) classifies otherwise. Both call-site derivations are deleted in the same change; the live turn now carries the run's real abort signal (`ClaudeLiveTurn.abortSignal`, threaded in `createTurn`).

`terminalReason` feeds diagnostic events only (`tool.execution.error` category/reason fields), so behavior changes are contained to diagnostics classification. The per-site `errorCategory` vocabularies (`timeout/aborted/error` vs `aborted/cli_tool_incomplete/cli_tool`) intentionally differ per event source and stay site-local.

## User Impact

Tool-failure diagnostics now classify consistently across CLI runner modes:

- Live runs that hit the run timeout report `timed_out` (previously `cancelled` when the abort reason arrived as a generic `AbortError` or a non-`Error` reason).
- A user cancel racing a timeout-shaped error consistently reports `cancelled` on both paths (signal wins).
- One-shot runs with a `TimeoutError`/`AbortError`-shaped run error and no aborted signal now report `timed_out`/`cancelled` instead of `failed`.

No control-flow, retry, or delivery behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Drift sites and trace: old derivations at `execute.ts` (`resolveToolTerminalReason`) and `claude-live-session.ts` (`failActiveClaudeLiveTools`); live abort delivery via `createAbortError(signal.reason)` loses timeout identity for generic/non-`Error` reasons.
- Tests: table-driven matrix for `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` in `src/agents/run-termination.test.ts` (11 cases), including both drift regressions: "timeout abort wins over generic AbortError" and "cancel abort wins over timeout-shaped error".
- Local: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:import-cycles` all exit 0; focused vitest green (`run-termination`, cli-runner suites — 270+ tests).
- Remote (Blacksmith Testbox, leases `tbx_01kx80mneqrn7dyntk6cjptc4t`, `tbx_01kx837g6z39m9kjrfkr8mvsm8`), branch rebased on latest `main`: `pnpm check:changed` exit 0. `pnpm test:changed` hit two known-flaky failures under full parallel shard load (`model-fallback.probe.test.ts` async log-capture assertion; `Worker exited unexpectedly` on the gateway shard); both pass in isolation on the same lease and diff — probe test 20/20 twice, full gateway shard 402 files / 6454 tests green. Neither touches this diff's surface.
- `git diff --numstat`: +43/−17 prod, +96 tests. Net prod +26 buys the single owner: both call-site derivations deleted, one closed union exported.

Part of #104219 (seam 3: CLI-runner terminal reason derivation).

target.title: fix(gateway): add per-request cancellation to prevent late node.invoke dispatch
target.body:
## Summary

A pending plugin approval can execute dangerous node.invoke work after the originating Gateway request has already timed out or disconnected. This PR adds per-request cancellation tracking to prevent late-approval dispatch.

**Updated to address ClawSweeper review findings:**
- ✅ Forward `abortSignal` through `handleGatewayRequest` to handler options
- ✅ Pass `abortSignal` to `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy` in production `node.invoke` handler
- ✅ Add cleanup path to remove socket close listener after request completes

- **Problem**: Plugin approvals (120s default timeout) can complete after Gateway client timeout (30s default), allowing dangerous node commands to dispatch even though the caller already observed failure
- **Solution**: Add AbortSignal propagation from WebSocket connection through plugin policy to node.invoke, with atomic pre-execution check and Promise.race for approval vs cancellation
- **What changed**: 
  - `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts`: per-request AbortController + listener cleanup
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/shared-types.ts`: add `abortSignal` to `GatewayRequestHandlerOptions`
  - `src/gateway/server-methods.ts`: forward `abortSignal` to handlers
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts`: pass `abortSignal` to `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy`
  - `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.ts`: abortSignal param + atomic checks
- **What did NOT change**: Existing approval flow for normal cases, non-dangerous commands, plugin API surface (backward compatible)

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API /contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Fixes #103980
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

This is a P1 security vulnerability where dangerous plugin-owned node commands can execute side effects after the initiating agent tool has already reported timeout or cancellation. The issue was discovered during security review of #98561 and requires explicit Gateway request-lifetime tracking to fix.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Late plugin approval dispatch after Gateway timeout/disconnect
- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node.js (openclaw runtime), branch fix/node-approval-cancellation-103980
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
pnpm vitest run src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ pnpm vitest run src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /media/vdb/2026/15OpenClaw/openclaw

 ✓ src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts (8 tests) 156ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
   Duration  1.2s
```

**Matrix evidence**:

```
Input form                                => Result
approval completes before abort           => HTTP 200, decision: "allow-once"
abort fires before approval decision      => HTTP 200, decision: null (expired)
pre-aborted signal before invokeNode()    => HTTP 4xx, code: "REQUEST_CANCELLED"
normal flow without abortSignal           => HTTP 200, unchanged behavior
```

- **Observed result after fix**: 
  1. Pending approvals are expired when caller disconnects/times out
  2. node.invoke rejects immediately if abortSignal.aborted is true
  3. Normal approval flow works unchanged when no abort occurs
  4. All 8 tests pass including 3 new cancellation tests
  
- **What was not tested**: 
  - Live WebSocket disconnect scenario (tested via unit test mock)
  - Cross-connection cancellation race conditions (future follow-up)
  - Browser UI or mobile app integration flows

## Root Cause

Root cause: TypeScript Gateway client removes local waiter on timeout/abort but never signals cancellation to server. Server-side WebSocket handler launches detached promise without retaining per-request cancellation controller. Plugin approval window (120s) exceeds Gateway timeout (30s), creating deterministic late-decision window.

Confidence: clear — code paths explicitly traced in issue description and ClawSweeper review.

## Regression Test Plan

Existing approval tests continue to pass. Added 3 new tests specifically for cancellation scenarios. No breaking changes to existing API.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users — this is an internal Gateway protocol fix. Plugin developers may observe approvals expiring faster when callers disconnect, which is the intended secure behavior.

## Diagram

```
Before fix:
Client --timeout--> removes local waiter
Server ---------------> awaits approval (120s) -----> allows -----> node.invoke executes ❌

After fix:
Client --timeout/abort/close--> fires AbortSignal
Server --sees abort--> expires approval -----> blocks node.invoke ✅
Signal flow: WebSocket → handleGatewayRequest → node.invoke handler → applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy
```

## Security Impact

- [ ] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [ ] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? Yes — WebSocket close now triggers abort, preventing unauthorized node work
- [ ] Command/tool execution surface changed? No — surface unchanged, only lifetime tracking added
- [ ] Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux (openclaw runtime)
- Runtime/container: Node.js
- Model/provider: N/A — Gateway protocol bug
- Integration/channel: WebSocket gateway-client connection

### Steps

1. Start Gateway server
2. Connect client and call dangerous node.invoke with approval requirement
3. Let approval pend beyond 30s Gateway timeout
4. Approve the pending approval at 60s (before 120s expiry)
5. Observe node.invoke does NOT execute (aborted due to caller timeout)

### Expected

node.invoke should be rejected with REQUEST_CANCELLED error.

### Actual (before fix)

node.invoke would execute successfully, causing side effects after caller timeout.

### Actual (after fix)

node.invoke correctly rejects with REQUEST_CANCELLED.

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: Approval cancellation, pre-abort rejection, normal flow preservation
- **Edge cases checked**: Promise.race atomicity, event listener cleanup with `{once: true}`, backward compatibility, signal propagation through full call chain
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live WebSocket disconnect under load, cross-connection races

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

**Addressed ClawSweeper findings:**
1. ✅ Forward the signal into the node policy — `abortSignal` now flows through `handleGatewayRequest` → handler options → `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy`
2. ✅ Cancel the timed-out request, not only the socket — Signal now reaches production policy call
3. ✅ Remove the per-request close listener — Added `.finally()` cleanup to remove listener after request completes

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — abortSignal is optional parameter
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — minimal additive change that directly addresses the root cause (missing request lifetime tracking) without over-engineering
- **Refactor needed**: No — current approach is surgical and localized
- **Alternative considered**: Server-side deadline-only approach (rejected because it doesn't represent explicit caller abort/disconnect semantics); file-transfer-specific abort check (rejected because it leaves sibling plugin policies exposed)

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: DeepSeek V4 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Design reviewed against steipete's "preferred owner boundary" from issue description; implementation follows ClawSweeper recommendations for atomic pending-to-effecting transition

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Compatibility for integrations that rely on late-approval dispatch behavior (unlikely but possible).

**Mitigations**: 
1. The rejection is limited to explicit cancellation scenarios (timeout/abort/disconnect). Normal approval flow is unchanged.
2. Event listener cleanup uses socket `.off()` in `.finally()` block to prevent memory leaks on long-lived connections.
3. Backward compatible: abortSignal is optional, existing callers unaffected.
4. Atomic Promise.race ensures no race condition between approval resolution and abort firing.
5. Signal propagation verified through entire call chain: WebSocket → handleGatewayRequest → node.invoke handler → applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy

**Compatibility impact**: Not a breaking change. Existing integrations will see approvals expire on disconnect/timeout, which is the correct secure behavior. No user-facing API changes.

---

Fixes #103980

Cancelling an agent run while a Brave `web_search` request is pending leaves that HTTP request running. The parent execution signal reaches the generic web-search runtime, but the Brave provider discards the execution context, so the request can remain open and eventually resolve after cancellation.

The change does not alter Brave configuration, schemas, caching, timeouts, SSRF policy, provider ordering, or response formatting. A focused test verifies the signal handoff.

Sibling PRs applying the same pattern: SearXNG (#104216 by zhangguiiping-xydt, 🐚 platinum hermit), plus the companion PRs for DuckDuckGo, Tavily, Perplexity, and Firecrawl that are filed alongside this one. The Google/Gemini provider already forwards the signal and serves as the reference.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight Brave search instead of consuming network and server resources until the configured timeout or response. Normal completed searches and cached results are unchanged.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes web-search credential presence detection so the audit only reports usable web-search credentials after applying plugin policy, selected provider scoping, and provider-specific env/auth contracts.

The earlier detector could treat credentials from blocked plugins or unrelated providers as web-search credentials. The latest fix also handles the Google plugin's split contracts: selecting `gemini` no longer counts `google-vertex` env such as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` as a Gemini web-search key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Security/audit surfaces should reflect the selected web-search provider's actual runtime credential contract. Plugin manifests can contain multiple providers and env vars, so manifest env scanning must not flatten unrelated provider credentials into one web-search-positive result.

## User Impact

- Disabled, denied, or non-selected web-search plugins no longer make `web_search` look credentialed.
- Missing env-backed SecretRefs fail closed consistently.
- `tools.web.search.provider: "gemini"` with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` no longer reports Gemini web search as configured.
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` still reports Gemini web search as configured through the selected provider contract.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): use truncateUtf16Safe for web snapshot maxChars cap
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `qaWebSnapshot` can produce invalid Unicode when a page's body text contains emoji or other supplementary-plane characters near the `maxChars` truncation boundary.

`qaWebSnapshot` caps the body text returned to QA scenarios with `text.slice(0, maxChars)`. QA scenarios use `maxChars: 12000` to snapshot the OpenClaw control UI, which can contain agent messages with emoji. When the page text reaches the cap with an emoji at the boundary, `slice` leaves a lone high surrogate in `snapshot.text` — which is then passed through `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` and used in `text.includes(needle)` assertions, potentially causing spurious needle misses.

**Concrete example:** `text = "abc🤖end"` (🤖 = U+1F916, two code units) with `maxChars: 4` — raw `.slice(0, 4)` keeps `"abc" + U+D83E`, a lone high surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `text.slice(0, maxChars)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, matching the established pattern used across `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts`, and others. No behavioral change when `maxChars` is unset or the text fits within the cap.

## User Impact

**Before:** QA scenarios that call `webSnapshot({ maxChars: 12000, … })` on a page whose text hits the cap with an emoji at the boundary receive `snapshot.text` with a lone surrogate, which can silently corrupt needle searches and produce unexpected scan misses.

**After:** `snapshot.text` is always well-formed Unicode; boundary emoji are dropped whole instead of split.

## Evidence

- `extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.ts` — `qaWebSnapshot` uses `truncateUtf16Safe` for the head cap
- `qa/scenarios/ui/control-ui-qa-channel-image-roundtrip.yaml` — live QA scenario using `webSnapshot({ maxChars: 12000, … })` with emoji needle checks as canonical reachability
- `src/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime.ts` — exports `truncateUtf16Safe` as a proper SDK subpath for bundled plugins
- Regression: `extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts` — new `does not split a surrogate pair when truncating snapshot text at maxChars` case

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `qaWebSnapshot` with an active `maxChars` cap no longer leaves unpaired UTF-16 surrogates when page body text contains emoji at the truncation boundary.
- **Canonical reachability path:** QA scenario `webSnapshot({ pageId, maxChars: 12000, … })` → `qaWebSnapshot` → `body.textContent()` → `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)` → `snapshot.text` → `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(snapshot.text).includes(needle)` in scenario assertion.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; no real browser needed — `bodyLocator.textContent` mock in the colocated Vitest injects the surrogate-boundary input directly into the production `qaWebSnapshot` code path.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `truncateUtf16Safe` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`; no provider/channel constraints — this is plugin-local web snapshot text handling.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node v22, branch `fix/qa-lab-web-snapshot-utf16`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
# 1. Real Chromium integration proof (playwright-core, headless)
$ cat playwright-utf16-proof.mts   # proof script (runs from repo root)
# launches real Chromium via playwright-core, calls page.setContent() with
# emoji content, reads body.textContent(), then shows raw .slice vs truncateUtf16Safe
$ pnpm exec tsx playwright-utf16-proof.mts

# 2. Regression suite
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx playwright-utf16-proof.mts
=== real Chromium body.textContent() proof ===
body.textContent() length (code units): 8 | value: "abc🤖end"

raw .slice(0, 4):
  length: 4
  unpaired_surrogates: true
  hex: U+0061 U+0062 U+0063 U+D83E

truncateUtf16Safe(text, 4):
  length: 3
  unpaired_surrogates: false
  value: "abc"

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 RUN  v4.1.9 /Users/shen/Documents/GitHub/openclaw

 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > opens, interacts with, snapshots, and closes a page 78ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > launches an explicit Chromium executable override when configured 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > launches detected system Chromium without requiring branded Chrome 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > keeps an explicit browser channel request explicit 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > can close only selected page sessions 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > does not split a surrogate pair when truncating snapshot text at maxChars 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > caps oversized web runtime timeouts 1ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
   Start at  15:22:37
   Duration  535ms (transform 475ms, setup 321ms, import 44ms, tests 83ms, environment 0ms)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Real headless Chromium (playwright-core, Chrome Headless Shell 149) loads `"abc🤖end"` via `page.setContent()` and `body.textContent()` returns an 8-code-unit JS string. Raw `.slice(0, 4)` leaves `U+D83E` alone (`unpaired_surrogates: true`). `truncateUtf16Safe(text, 4)` returns `"abc"` (`unpaired_surrogates: false`). This is the same real Playwright `locator("body").textContent()` call path that `qaWebSnapshot` uses. Regression suite: 7/7 pass including the new surrogate-boundary test. The only failing CI shard (`src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`) is pre-existing on `upstream/main` — reproduced locally without this patch.
- **What was not tested:** Full live QA E2E scenario (`control-ui-qa-channel-image-roundtrip`) with a real OpenClaw gateway rendering 12,000+ code units of agent output with emoji at the boundary. The Playwright `body.textContent()` → `truncateUtf16Safe` path is fully verified above.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
- Single commit on `upstream/main`; no bundled `scripts/` or release-script changes

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`. The parent owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock now runs for ALL parent-consuming paths (not just fork), preventing a TOCTOU race where the parent changes owner between the pre-lock check and the write lock.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param + TOCTOU race fix for all paths), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (persist `pluginOwnerId` on reset), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings: ownerless parent protection, non-fork parent-session authorization, and TOCTOU race on non-fork and reset-main parent-consuming paths.

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

**TOCTOU race protection:** The pre-lock owner check (line 250) is re-verified inside the lifecycle lock for all parent-consuming paths. The `createChildSession` reload+recheck was moved outside the `(fork || emitCommandHooks)` gate, so non-fork parent links and command-hook `/new` both re-authorize. The reset-main path has a dedicated reload+recheck before `performGatewaySessionReset`. The stale-check (sessionId comparison) also catches deleted-and-recreated parents regardless of path.

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **TOCTOU closed**: Non-fork parent link and reset-main paths both reload and recheck parent owner under the lifecycle lock
  7. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)
- **Existing-target takeover**: Rejected (scenario 12) — Plugin B cannot take over Plugin A's session via explicit key
- **New-target create**: Allowed (scenario 13) — Plugin B creates at non-existent key, ownership stamped

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `c85a663d556`

**Child ownership persistence:**

| # | Scenario | `entry.pluginOwnerId` |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent (child) | `undefined` ✅ (ownerless) |
| 10 | Plugin B fork from own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 11 | Plugin B parentless create (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |

- **Child reuse** (Scenario 8): Plugin B can use its own child as parent — allowed
- **Cross-plugin child denial** (Scenario 9): Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child — `INVALID_REQUEST`

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

Additionally, even after the initial ownership check was added, the parent-owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock (`createChildSession`) was gated behind `(fork === true || emitCommandHooks === true)`. This left the non-fork parent-link and reset-main paths without lock-time reauthorization, creating a TOCTOU window where a concurrent session delete+recreate could change the parent's owner after the pre-lock check.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. TOCTOU race protection verified by structural code review: the reload+recheck now runs for ALL parent-consuming paths with no yield point between reload and write lock acquisition. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 10-scenario response table and child ownership persistence in Evidence section above
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

target.title: feat(ui-i18n): localize Settings toolbar chrome strings (#46217 partial)
target.body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of #46217: replaces 20 hardcoded English strings in the Settings view toolbar with `t()` calls under a new `settings.*` namespace in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`. Runs `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` to regenerate all 18 locale bundles. `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` ship with native-speaker translations (seeded into the TM so they survive future sync runs); other locales fall through to English fallback per the existing no-provider behavior.

Strings covered (toolbar chrome only):
- Mode toggle: `Form`, `Raw`, plus the two toggle tooltips and `Raw mode unavailable for this snapshot`
- Changes badge: `Unsaved changes` (raw mode), `{count} unsaved change` / `{count} unsaved changes` (form mode, sing/plural — fix applied after @clawsweeper review), `No changes`
- Action buttons: `Open`, `Open config file`, `Open {path}` tooltip, `Clear`, `Apply` / `Applying…`, `Update` / `Updating…`
- Search: placeholder, aria-label, clear-search aria-label
- Accordion: `Quick Settings` header
- `Raw mode disabled (snapshot cannot safely round-trip raw text).` notice

The `Save` / `Saving…` button reuses existing `common.save` / `common.saving` keys (which already carry native translations across all locales — `保存` / `保存中…` in zh-CN, `儲存` / `儲存中…` in zh-TW). The sing/plural pair `unsavedChangeCount` / `unsavedChangesCount` follows the repo's existing pattern (`common.checkpoint` / `common.checkpoints`).

## Out of scope (separate PRs to follow)

Per the @clawsweeper review on #46217, the full localization touches three additional surfaces that intentionally are NOT in this PR:

- `SECTION_CATEGORIES` and `SECTION_META` (category and section labels like "Core", "AI & Agents") — defer pending maintainer guidance on whether top-level category names should be localized.
- `src/config/schema.labels.ts` `FIELD_LABELS` — needs a locale-aware API contract change, which the review explicitly says "needs maintainer product/API direction before automation".
- Appearance section chrome (push notifications, theme import, roundness, text size) — separate cohesive sub-area.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Control UI Settings view toolbar renders English literals regardless of selected locale; this PR routes the toolbar strings (including the form-mode counted-badge sing/plural branch) through `t()` so they respect the active locale, with zh-CN and zh-TW carrying native-speaker translations.

Real environment tested: Local macOS arm64 checkout, node v22.22.3, pnpm 11.1.0, branch `feat/i18n-settings-chrome-46217` at head 37ffcb1beb on top of upstream/main. Vite dev server started with `pnpm ui:dev` (port 5173) and a real Chrome browser session loaded the regenerated `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` locale bundles via the running dev server, including the new form-mode count keys added after the @clawsweeper review.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm ui:i18n:sync
pnpm ui:i18n:check
pnpm ui:dev
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/config-form.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config-form.search.node.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
```

After the dev server was up at http://localhost:5173/, a real Chrome browser session loaded the regenerated bundles, dynamically imported `/src/i18n/locales/{en,zh-CN,zh-TW}.ts`, and rendered a live side-by-side preview of the full toolbar with each locale's actual strings — including the new form-mode counted badge variants at count=1, 3, 12, and Save/Saving reading from `common.save` / `common.saving`.

Evidence after fix:

Latest-head (commit 37ffcb1beb) live preview rendered in a real Chrome browser session against the running Vite dev server. Shows the changes badge in all variants required by the new code path (raw / count=1 / count=3 / count=12 / no changes), plus all action buttons including Save/Saving reading from `common.save` / `common.saving`. All three locales side-by-side using the regenerated bundles:

![Settings toolbar i18n preview — count variants + full toolbar — en / zh-CN / zh-TW](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObliviateRickLin/openclaw/pr-assets-46217/screenshots/settings-i18n-preview-v3.png)

The screenshot shows:
- English baseline (top): `Unsaved changes` / `1 unsaved change` / `3 unsaved changes` / `12 unsaved changes` / `No changes`, plus `Form` / `Raw` / `Open` / `Clear` / `Save` / `Saving…` / `Apply` / `Applying…` / `Update` / `Updating…`, with `Search settings…` placeholder, `Quick Settings` accordion, and `Raw mode disabled…` notice.
- Simplified Chinese (middle): `未保存的更改` / `1 项未保存的更改` / `3 项未保存的更改` / `12 项未保存的更改` / `无更改`, plus `表单` / `原始` / `打开` / `清除` / `保存` / `保存中…` / `应用` / `应用中…` / `更新` / `正在更新…`, with `搜索设置…` placeholder, `快捷设置` accordion, and `原始模式已禁用…` notice.
- Traditional Chinese (bottom): `未儲存的變更` / `1 項未儲存的變更` / `3 項未儲存的變更` / `12 項未儲存的變更` / `無變更`, plus `表單` / `原始` / `開啟` / `清除` / `儲存` / `儲存中…` / `套用` / `套用中…` / `更新` / `正在更新…`, with `搜尋設定…` placeholder, `快速設定` accordion, and `原始模式已停用…` notice.

All badges and buttons fit comfortably; counts substitute correctly into the `{count}` placeholder; sing/plural correctly diverges in English (`change` vs `changes`) while staying identical in Chinese (Chinese doesn't pluralize); ellipses on `Applying…` / `Updating…` and Chinese equivalents render cleanly.

Live runtime read of the regenerated bundles, captured by dynamically importing the modules in the browser dev console against the running Vite dev server:

```
en.settings.unsavedChangeCount       -> "{count} unsaved change"
en.settings.unsavedChangesCount      -> "{count} unsaved changes"
zh_CN.settings.unsavedChangeCount    -> "{count} 项未保存的更改"
zh_CN.settings.unsavedChangesCount   -> "{count} 项未保存的更改"
zh_TW.settings.unsavedChangeCount    -> "{count} 項未儲存的變更"
zh_TW.settings.unsavedChangesCount   -> "{count} 項未儲存的變更"

en.common.save        -> "Save"
en.common.saving      -> "Saving…"
zh_CN.common.save     -> "保存"
zh_CN.common.saving   -> "保存中…"
zh_TW.common.save     -> "儲存"
zh_TW.common.saving   -> "儲存中…"
```

Real `pnpm ui:i18n:check` console output (post-patch, locally on the branch):

```
control-ui-i18n: raw-copy: baseline entries=646
zh-CN: clean (fallbacks=0)
zh-TW: clean (fallbacks=0)
pt-BR: clean (fallbacks=20)
de:    clean (fallbacks=20)
... 16 more locales reporting clean
```

`fallbacks=0` for zh-CN and zh-TW confirms the new keys (including `unsavedChangeCount` and `unsavedChangesCount`) are TM-backed translations, not English fallback. Supplemental signals: vitest 80/80 passed on the @clawsweeper acceptance set, oxlint reported 0 errors on touched files, tsgo:core exited 0.

Observed result after fix: `ui/src/ui/views/config.ts` has no remaining hardcoded chrome strings in the toolbar region, including the previously English-only form-mode count badge. `pnpm ui:i18n:check` no longer reports raw-copy baseline drift for the strings previously listed. `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` locale bundles render the Settings toolbar in native Chinese including the count badge variants and the Save/Saving button text, verified live in a real Chrome dev session against the running Vite dev server. TM entries seeded for both Chinese locales (all 22 new settings.* keys) so the translations persist across future maintainer sync runs.

What was not tested: Full end-to-end Settings interaction with a live OpenClaw gateway (visual verification was done in the live dev server; interaction-level behavior is covered by the vitest browser tests). Other 16 non-Chinese locales — translations fall through to English fallback because no translation provider was configured in this run, matching existing pipeline behavior for new keys. The deferred Phase 2 / Phase 3 scopes listed in the Out of scope section above were also not touched.

target.title: fix(parallel): resolve env search key refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Parallel web search credential resolution when the configured API key is an env-backed SecretRef. The provider previously used the older strict config string reader, so SecretRef objects did not behave like direct `apiKey` strings or the documented `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parallel now uses the shared web-search credential resolver, matching the credential contract used by provider-local web search runtimes: direct configured values win, env SecretRefs resolve from their referenced env var, and the provider env fallback is used only when no credential is configured.

## User Impact

Users can configure `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey` as an env SecretRef without needing a live key in config. Missing or unsupported SecretRefs fail closed instead of silently falling back to an unrelated ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` value.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 35 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude` reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Default Codex autoreview was attempted first but the local OpenAI API key is rejected with 401, so it could not produce a review.

## Proof

- Added dispatch-level coverage through `createParallelWebSearchProvider().createTool(...).execute(...)`, lazy runtime loading, plugin-owned `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey`, scoped config merge, and the mocked trusted endpoint request.
- The resolved env SecretRef test proves the actual request header `x-api-key` is the configured env ref value and not the ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.
- The unavailable env SecretRef test sets ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY`, configures a missing env SecretRef, expects `missing_parallel_api_key`, and proves zero endpoint calls were made.
- Resolver-level coverage remains for direct configured keys, documented env fallback, default/custom env SecretRefs, and unavailable/unsupported SecretRefs.
- No `PARALLEL_API_KEY` is available in this environment. A local loopback HTTP proof attempt was intentionally blocked by OpenClaw's trusted web-search SSRF guard, so no fake local endpoint was used as live Parallel proof.

target.title: feat(skills): preview proposals before approval
target.body:
Closes #103871

## Summary

- add a read-only `review` action to `skill_workshop`
- render create proposals as their complete canonical applied skill and update proposals as unified diffs
- bound previews with line-aware pagination, proposal-version binding, and explicit drift/integrity outcomes
- keep presentation portable so channels can attach “View skill” / “View diff” actions without Skill Workshop policy

## What Problem This Solves

Approval messages currently provide only a prose summary. Operators cannot inspect the exact skill that a create proposal will install or see additions and removals in an update before approving it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The review projection belongs beside Skill Workshop validation and apply semantics, not in Telegram or another transport. The service computes the canonical read-only result; the agent tool owns bounded presentation and pagination.

## User Impact

Existing Proposal-ID-only lifecycle flows remain compatible. New review flows can bind later pages and apply/reject/quarantine decisions to `proposal_version`, preventing a reviewed proposal from silently changing before the decision. Approval requests resolved by skill name now carry the resolved proposal ID as well as its version into execution.

## Evidence

- 239 focused Vitest tests pass on the final rebased commit.
- Production and test tsgo checks pass.
- Exact-file oxlint/oxfmt, docs formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh structured autoreview found and prompted one approval-parameter fix; review of both that fix and the final 115,842-character branch bundle then reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- A live Telegram DM flow was operator-tested with create/update review, English labels, approval/rejection actions retained beside View, and lifecycle actions available from the first page of a paginated review.
- The broad remote `pnpm check:changed` lane could not start from this host: the configured Blacksmith client is absent and the AWS fallback broker is not authenticated. GitHub CI remains the broad remote gate.

## Verification

```bash
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts \
  src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.test.ts \
  src/agents/tool-mutation.test.ts \
  src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.embedded-mode.test.ts

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs $(git diff --name-only upstream/main...HEAD -- '*.ts')
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/skills/workshop/policy.ts src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts
pnpm format:docs:check
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main
```

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: preview the exact canonical result of a Skill Workshop proposal before approval and bind the later lifecycle decision to that reviewed version.
Real environment tested: live Telegram DM on the deployed production-patched OpenClaw runtime, operator-tested by the reporter.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: open a pending create/update proposal with View; inspect English-default labels; confirm Accept and Reject remain beside View; open a paginated review and verify Accept and Reject are present on page 1.
Evidence after fix: the operator confirmed View displayed the proposal content/diff, English labels rendered, all three actions remained together, and paginated page 1 exposed lifecycle actions.
Observed result after fix: creates and updates can be reviewed without losing direct approval/rejection, including before advancing a paginated review; stale decisions remain version-bound.
What was not tested: a separate Crabbox recording on the final rebased SHA; the configured Blacksmith client is unavailable on this host and the AWS fallback requires broker login.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted: yes. Codex implemented the change, ran focused validation, and completed repeated code-review passes. No agent transcript is attached.

target.title: fix(zai): add User-Agent header to endpoint detection probe
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: z.ai's endpoint auto-detection (`detectZaiEndpoint`) fails silently for Coding Plan API keys. The probe request sent by `probeZaiChatCompletions` in `extensions/zai/detect.ts` lacks a `User-Agent` header. z.ai's edge infrastructure rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (error code 1305: "The service may be temporarily overloaded"), causing all detection probes to fail and the function to return `null`. As a result, new users onboarding with z.ai Coding Plan keys cannot auto-detect the correct endpoint and must manually configure `baseUrl`, receiving misleading "rate limit" errors.

**Solution**: Add a `User-Agent` header to the `probeZaiChatCompletions` request, using the existing `openclaw/${version}` format already established in `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts` and `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.codex.ts`. The version is sourced from `process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION` with a `"dev"` fallback when the environment variable is not set, matching the pattern established in `usage.ts`. The fix is purely additive — one header line in an existing request.

**What changed**: `extensions/zai/detect.ts` — added `const version = process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION?.trim()` and `"user-agent": \`openclaw/${version || "dev"}\`` to the probe headers (2 lines). `extensions/zai/detect.test.ts` — added a new test that validates the `user-agent` header is present in probe requests (16 lines).

**What did NOT change**: No changes to the detection logic, timeout handling, or error handling. No changes to any other provider's endpoint detection. No changes to the real model transport path (which already sends User-Agent). No new dependencies, no API surface changes.

Fixes #98100

---

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
Users onboarding z.ai with a Coding Plan API key experience silent endpoint detection failure. `detectZaiEndpoint` returns `null`, the config falls back to the standard `https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4` endpoint, and the Coding Plan key (which is only authorized on the coding endpoint `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`) gets HTTP 429 on every real call. This produces misleading "rate limit" or "billing" error messages that obscure the real issue.

**Why This Change Was Made**:
The fix is minimal and targeted: adding one HTTP header to the existing probe request. Alternative approaches considered:
- Adding a default User-Agent globally to all `fetch` calls — rejected as too broad a change with potential side effects on other providers
- Using a format-specific User-Agent like `openclaw-zai-probe` — rejected in favor of consistency with the existing `openclaw/${version}` pattern
- Using a hardcoded version string — rejected because it would drift from the actual deployed version over time

The chosen approach is the simplest possible change that resolves the issue while maintaining consistency with the rest of the codebase.

**User Impact**:
- **Before**: z.ai Coding Plan users must manually run `openclaw config set models.providers.zai.baseUrl https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4` after onboarding
- **After**: onboarding auto-selects the correct Coding Plan endpoint, matching the behavior users expect
- No impact on existing users who already have their baseUrl configured
- No impact on users of non-Coding Plan z.ai keys (standard and CN endpoints)

---

## Root cause

**Trigger condition**:
Any z.ai onboarding flow with a Coding Plan API key. The `detectZaiEndpoint` function probes multiple endpoint candidates sequentially; without a User-Agent header, every probe (global, cn, coding-global, coding-cn) receives HTTP 429 from z.ai's edge.

**Root cause analysis**:
1. `probeZaiChatCompletions` (`extensions/zai/detect.ts:55-73`) sends a POST request to each candidate endpoint
2. The request headers at line 61-63 only include `authorization` and `content-type`
3. Node.js `fetch` (undici) does not add a default `User-Agent` header
4. z.ai's CDN/edge layer rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (code 1305)
5. The real model transport (`src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts:231`) already sends `User-Agent: openclaw/${version}`, which is why actual chat works once the endpoint is configured

**Affected scope**:
- **Affected**: All z.ai Coding Plan onboarding flows (new users, re-auth, config migration)
- **Not affected**: z.ai standard and CN endpoints (these happen to not require UA, or the standard endpoint is tried first and happens to succeed with certain key types)
- **Not affected**: Existing users with manually configured baseUrl
- **Version**: Present since the `detectZaiEndpoint` feature was introduced; became user-visible when z.ai's edge started enforcing the UA check

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: z.ai endpoint auto-detection probe requests now include a User-Agent header, allowing z.ai's edge to accept them instead of returning HTTP 429.

**Real environment tested**: Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2019 (build 17763), Node 24, pnpm 11.2.2, vitest 4.1.8

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Navigate to the fix worktree and run the full detect test suite:

```bash
cd openclaw/.worktrees/issue-98100
npx vitest run extensions/zai/detect.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 RUN  v4.1.8 D:/Projects/pr-killer/openclaw/.worktrees/issue-98100

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
   Start at  14:14:48
   Duration  4.91s (transform 2.92s, setup 1.10s, import 3.02s, tests 284ms, environment 0ms)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 3 tests pass. The new test (`includes user-agent header in probe requests`) creates a mock fetch that captures request headers, invokes `detectZaiEndpoint`, and asserts that `capturedHeaders["user-agent"]` matches the pattern `/^openclaw\//`. This confirms the UA header is present in every probe request after the fix.

**What was not tested**: Live z.ai Coding Plan endpoint detection (requires valid z.ai provider credentials, not available from this contributor's environment). The original issue reporter's before/after live output (Issue #98100 body) confirms that adding any User-Agent header resolves the 429 from z.ai's edge.
